newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Buthelezi sworn in as S.Africa's acting president.
newsitem.headline: Buthelezi sworn in as S.Africa's acting president.

text.p: South Africa's Zulu leader Mangosuthu Buthelezi was sworn in as acting president on Saturday and said the trust shown in him by President Nelson Mandela during an absence abroad would reconcile their rival parties.
In a brief ceremony in the Indian Ocean port city of Durban Buthelezi swore to run the country while Mandela and his deputy Thabo Mbeki attend next week's World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland.

"I really thank the president for the trust and confidence he has shown in me...I see this as a gesture towards reconciliation between our parties because we are parties in conflict with each other," Buthelezi told reporters after the ceremony.

Buthelezi, the 68-year-old leader of the Zulu-based Inkatha Freedom Party, is the interior minister in South Africa's unity government but is one of the fiercest critics of Mandela's ruling African National Congress.
Inkatha has been fighting a bloody turf war against the ANC in KwaZulu-Natal, home to nine million Zulus, for over a decade. The fighting has killed and displaced thousands of people.
Analysts and politicians believe Mandela's conciliatory gesture to his oldest enemy could help normalise relations between the two parties.
ANC chairman Jacob Zuma, who attended the ceremony, said peace in in KwaZulu-Natal could be bolstered by the confidence shown in Buthelezi.
"This will go a long way in contributing to the efforts we are making to bring peace and stability to KwaZulu-Natal and the country," Zuma said.

He said the ANC was preparing a peace package to present to Inkatha. Part of the plan could include a special amnesty deal for those involved in the political violence that flared after Mandela's inauguration in May 1994.
A Durban-based political analyst said the move by Mandela was shrewd because it would force Buthelezi to respond in a positive way.
Numerous attempts to get both leaders to share a platform to preach peace in KwaZulu-Natal since the 1994 elections have failed with each blaming the other for not doing enough.
